newsitem.title: USA: Don Sancho says Clinton needs more beans in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Don Sancho says Clinton needs more beans in Texas.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is leading Republican challenger Bob Dole in the national opinion polls but in Texas he needs more beans.

So says Don Sancho, the venerable pollster in this island city who admittedly is a dummy, but who for the past five elections has correctly predicted how the presidential vote would go in the Lone Star state.

The latest weekly count in Don Sancho's Presidential Frijole Poll shows that Dole has 1,050 beans, or 48 percent, to 895, or 41 percent, for Clinton. Texas billionaire Ross Perot is way behind with just 245 beans, or 3 percent.
Frijole is Tex-Mex for the Spanish word "frijol," or bean.

The Don Sancho poll is slightly unorthodox. Customers at Mama Ninfa's Mexican food restaurant vote by placing pinto beans in wine carafes marked for each candidate. The bean-counting started in late September.

Dole held just a four-bean lead over Clinton early on but after the first presidential debate he widened the gap to 100 beans and has gained strength ever since. "For Dole to jump to a 100-bean lead in one short week, (the) debate must have had an impact," said Chip DeMoss, spokesman for Don Sancho.

Don Sancho does not have much to say because he is a wooden mannequin. Wearing a big sombrero, a droopy moustache and an unwavering smile, he sits in eternal vigilance at the polling table in Mama Ninfa's in Galveston's historic Strand district. His bean polls began in 1976 at the now-defunct Corella's restaurant when owner Manuel Corella was looking for a way to attract customers.

In beans, Corella found truth. Jimmy Carter won the first poll and also became the last Democratic presidential candidate to carry Texas. Since then, Republicans have dominated the poll, just as they have the real ballot box.

Corella closed his restaurant a couple of years ago, so it looked like Don Sancho had polled his last. But the old dummy, by now a Galveston institution, was taken out of mothballs and placed at Mama Ninfa's for the 1996 election, DeMoss said.

The new location does not appear to have affected the predictive power of Don Sancho's beans. Even though Clinton has not publicly written off vote-rich Texas, Dole is so confident of victory he has barely campaigned here.
Professional polls differ little from Don Sancho's. One recent survey showed Dole leading by 50-41 percent in Texas, with Perot a very distant third. Others show Dole ahead by a smaller margin.
"The thing about Don Sancho is it's fun, but it's serious. It's like a thermometer -- Don Sancho tells the truth," said Mama Ninfa's manager Franklin Ochoa.
